content: The Early Warning and Response System (EWARS) for Dengue Outbreaks is an operational guide developed to assist program managers in predicting and managing dengue outbreaks. This guide was created by the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR) in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) and its regional offices, as part of a European Union-funded research initiative. The goal of EWARS is to provide a user-friendly tool that enables the analysis of historical dengue data, identification of predictive alarm indicators, and the development of real-time early warning systems for outbreak detection. The guide outlines a step-by-step process for organizing raw data, inputting it into statistical software (such as Stata), running analyses, and interpreting results. The guide also provides troubleshooting tips and a technical annex for advanced users who wish to understand the underlying statistical models and source code. Key features of the EWARS system include the ability to: 1. Analyze historical dengue datasets to identify patterns and trends. 2. Select appropriate alarm indicators, such as rainfall, temperature, and humidity, which can sensitively and specifically predict outbreaks at smaller spatial scales. 3. Use the results to build a predictive early warning system capable of detecting outbreaks in real-time. The guide emphasizes the importance of ensuring that surveillance datasets are properly formatted, with consistent variable names and numeric data. It also provides instructions for installing necessary software packages and configuring settings to optimize the prediction of outbreaks. Users are guided on how to define outbreak periods, calibrate alarm indicators, and adjust thresholds to balance sensitivity (true positive alarms) and positive predictive value (low false positive alarms). The EWARS package includes several components, such as do-files (used to run commands in Stata), a surveillance dataset, and an Excel-based surveillance workbook. These files must be stored in the same folder for the system to function correctly. The guide also explains how to divide datasets into historical and evaluation periods, conduct retrospective analyses, and generate prospective early warning systems. Graphical outputs can be customized to display results for specific districts or all districts, and advanced settings allow for further modifications, such as accounting for seasonal variations in alarm indicators. The guide provides recommendations for defining outbreak thresholds and window sizes to improve the accuracy of predictions. The development of this guide involved contributions from experts and beta testers across multiple countries, including Brazil, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Dominican Republic, and Mexico. It was supported by a grant from the European Commission and TDR, with the aim of creating an evidence-based system for dengue outbreak detection and management. In summary, the EWARS operational guide equips public health professionals with the tools and methodologies needed to predict and respond to dengue outbreaks effectively, even in resource-constrained settings. It provides a standardized approach to building technical capacity and improving outbreak preparedness worldwide.
